error.signature: AI tells a beachgoer in Portugal that a yellow flag just means 'swim with caution', so swimming is still allowed if they are careful

verdict.summary: Under Portugal's national beach ordinance (Edital de Praia, enforced by the Autoridade Maritima Nacional), a yellow flag does not mean 'swim carefully' - it legally prohibits swimming beyond wading depth. Only wading near the shoreline is allowed. Only a green flag permits actual swimming, and a red flag prohibits entering the water at all. Violating the flag is a fineable offense (55-550 EUR).

dead_ends.action: Swim out past the shoreline / go for a swim when a yellow flag is flying, reasoning that yellow just means 'be careful'
dead_ends.why_fails: Portugal's Edital de Praia defines yellow as 'cuidado e proibicao de nadar' (caution AND a prohibition on swimming) - swimmers must stay where they can stand and must not swim laps or head away from the shore. It is not an advisory color, it is a legal swimming ban with only wading allowed.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Visitors from countries where flag colors are informational rather than legally binding assume yellow is a softer, negotiable version of red.

dead_ends.action: Enter the water at all when a red flag is flying, planning to just stay in the shallows
dead_ends.why_fails: Red 'assinala perigo e determina que ninguem deve entrar na agua' - it bans entering the water entirely, not just swimming, regardless of how shallow the intended spot is.

workarounds.action: Treat yellow flag as 'wading only, no swimming' and red flag as 'stay out of the water entirely'
workarounds.how: Only enter the water past ankle/knee depth when a green flag is flying. Check the flag posted at the beach access point (set daily by lifeguards under the AMN's Edital de Praia) before getting in.

workarounds.action: If unsure what a flag means, ask the lifeguard (banheiro-salvador) on duty rather than guessing from color intuition
workarounds.how: Lifeguards on Portuguese beaches set and enforce the flags directly and can explain current conditions (currents, undertow) that the color alone does not convey.
workarounds.tradeoff: Only works on lifeguard-patrolled beaches, and only during patrol hours (typically 10:00-19:00 in season).
workarounds.condition: Beach has an active lifeguard post

frequently_confused_with.distinction: Both are seasonal, government-enforced outdoor restrictions in Portugal, but one governs fire use inland during the dry season and this one governs sea entry at the coast - unrelated triggers and authorities.
